primary.title: EnBW Case Study: Autonomous Drones for Gigawatt Solar Portfolio | FlytBase
primary.why_strongest_fit: EnBW is one of Germany's largest energy companies, so it is the closest peer to E.ON among FlytBase's published customers. The site has no substation or line case study, but EnBW shows the same operating model E.ON is asking for: docked drones (DJI Dock 2 on FlytBase) running routine thermal inspection across dispersed remote energy assets in place of people travelling to site. It deals with the Germany-specific obstacles E.ON's Bavarian team will meet, namely unpredictable weather that makes thermal flight windows hard to schedule, grid curtailment, and terrain with line-of-sight problems. It also started as a two-dock proof of concept, which matches the pilot proposal E.ON's procurement wants by January.
key_proof_points: Solar portfolio grew 'from 150 MW to 1 GW in just four years'
Increased inspection frequency 'from annual to quarterly monitoring'
'Eliminated six-hour round trips to remote sites'
'The proof-of-concept deployment with two operational docks is paving the way for autonomous operations across EnBW's entire gigawatt-scale solar portfolio'
Stack: 'DJI Dock 2 hardware with FlytBase's automation platform and Sitemark's AI analytics'
Before docks, 'pilots traveling two to six hours to remote sites often arrived to find conditions unsuitable for flying'
primary.how_to_use_it: Use it as the German peer proof point in the first reply: 'another large German energy company moved routine thermal inspection to docked drones and went from annual to quarterly inspections without adding headcount'. Present the two-dock PoC as the template for E.ON's January pilot proposal (for example 1-2 docks at representative Bavarian substations). Say plainly that the EnBW assets are solar PV, not substations, so the claim stays honest, and use it to open a discussion of substation-specific missions, BVLOS approval in Germany and data integration.

secondary.title: Hydropower Monitoring with Autonomous Drones | FlytBase
secondary.why: A DACH utility (Axpo, Switzerland's largest sustainable energy producer) using DJI Dock 2 for routine inspection of remote energy infrastructure in harsh Alpine weather. The page covers health and safety, permits and aviation-safety (FLARM) integration and says Axpo plans to expand to grid infrastructure. Use it for the regulatory and operational-readiness discussion around BVLOS. TNB (S2) can be added as the only page that mentions substations, though only as a planned deployment.
